# **Data Summary**

This project uses three datasets from O*NET that contain occupation descriptions, task statements, and skill ratings. The original data sets included 1,016 occupations, 18,838 tasks, and 18,200 skill ratings. The O*NET-SOC Codes were used to link the datasets together.

Of the intial 1,016 occupations, 910 were represented across all 3 data sets and were retained for analysis. Within each occupation, the task statements were grouped, the 5 highest rated skills by importance were selected, and all other details were combined into a single career profile.

The final processed file, career_profiles.csv, contains 910 unique occupations that have been limited to 384 tokens using the all-mpnet-base-v2 tokenizer so that the data can be used with Sentence-Bert analysis.

# **Provenance**

The data used in this project come from the ONET 31.0 Database, maintained by the U.S. Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration. The occupation dataset provides each occupation's O*NET-SOC code, title, and description; the task dataset provides occupation-specific task statements; and the essential-skills dataset provides skill names and associated ratings.

For this project, the original O*NET files were filtered and reorganized into a single processed dataset. Occupations were matched across files using O*NET-SOC Codes, incomplete occupations were excluded, task statements were grouped by occupation, and the five highest-rated skills by importance were retained for each career profile. The processed data were then formatted for use with the Sentence-BERT model.

This license allows the data to be copied, modified, and redistributed for this project as long as appropriate credit is given to O*NET and the U.S. Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration, the license is identified, and any changes made to the original data are indicated.

The processed career_profiles.csv file is derived from the original O*NET data and should therefore retain the same attribution requirements when reused or shared.

# **Ethical Statements**

This project involves privacy and fairness concerns. User resumes may contain personally identifiable information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, or email addresses, so unnecessary identifying information should be removed before the resume is processed by the model.

The project also recognizes that O*NET data and resume data may reflect existing biases in education and employment. These biases could affect which careers are recommended or overlooked. For this reason, the system should be treated as a career recommendation tool rather than a definitive prediction of what career a person should pursue.

# **Data Dictionary**

O = occupation_data.csv  
T = task_statements.csv  
S = essential_skills.csv  
P = career_profiles.csv

| Feature / Column | Description | Type / Format | Example / Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| O*NET-SOC Code (O,T,S,P) | Occupational identifier linking files | Text Identifier | `11-1011.00` |
| Title (O,T,S,P) | Official occupation name | Text | `Chief Executives` |
| Description (O,P) | Summary of occupation responsibilities | Text | `Determine and formulate policies...` |
| Task ID (T) | Identifier for a task | Integer Identifier | `8823` |
| Task (T) | Description of an individual occupation task | Text | `Coordinate business activities...` |
| Task Type (T) | Core or supplemental task classification | Categorical Text | Some missing values |
| Incumbents Responding (T) | Number of workers providing task information | Numeric | Some missing values |
| Domain Source (T,S) | Information source | Categorical Text | Incumbent, analyst, etc. |
| Element ID (S) | Skill identifier | Text Identifier | `2.A.1.a` |
| Element Name (S) | Name of skill | Text | `Reading Comprehension` |
| Scale ID (S) | Identifier for ratings scale | Categorical Text | `IM` = Importance |
| Scale Name (S) | Full name of rating scale | Categorical Text | Importance or Level |
| Data Value (S) | Mean skill rating | Numeric | `4.12` on importance |
| N (S) | Number of analysts contributing to rating | Integer Count | Varies by rating |
| Recommend Suppress (S) | Flags low-precision ratings | Boolean / Categorical | `N` = not flagged, `Y` = suppress |
| Not Relevant (S) | Flags ratings that are not relevant | Boolean / Categorical | `Y` = not relevant, `N` = not flagged |
| Tasks (P) | All available task statements grouped for an occupation | Text | Task statements separated by `\|` |
| Task_Count (P) | Number of task statements originally available for the occupation | Integer | `31` for Chief Executives |
| Skills (P) | Five skills with the highest importance ratings for the occupation | Text | `Critical Thinking \| Speaking \| ...` |
| Skill_Importance (P) | Importance ratings corresponding to the five selected skills | Text / Numeric List | `4.38 \| 4.25 \| 4.12 \| ...` |
| Skill_Count (P) | Number of skills retained for the career profile | Integer | `5` for all occupations |
| Final_Career_Profile (P) | Combined title, description, retained tasks, and selected skills used as Sentence-BERT input | Text | Standardized text profile |
| Final_Token_Count (P) | Number of `all-mpnet-base-v2` tokenizer tokens in the final profile | Integer | Maximum of `384` |
| Tasks_Used (P) | Number of complete task statements included in the final profile | Integer | `13` for Chief Executives |
| Tasks_Dropped (P) | Number of task statements omitted to remain within the token limit | Integer | `18` for Chief Executives |
